context: Monday 30 November: アルちゃん goes to {長野市|ながのし} by train to buy gloves and goggles for the ski day, takes a taxi in the snow, and on the way home thinks about レン, who lives in the same city.
scene: You tell the story of your Monday trip to {長野市|ながのし}: a taxi ride in the snow, and a message you didn't send.

phrases.jp: この{住所|じゅうしょ|address|3}までお{願い|ねがい}します。
phrases.note: Show the address on your phone. Drivers will also ask どちらまで？

phrases.jp: {次|つぎ}の{信号|しんごう|traffic light|4}で{止めて|とめて|to stop (something)|4}もらえますか。
phrases.en: Could you stop at the next light?
phrases.note: 〜てもらえますか = polite request. Also: ここでいいです (here is fine).

phrases.jp: カードで{払えますか|はらえますか}。
phrases.note: Ask before you get in: country taxis don't always take cards.

phrases.jp: {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ|receipt|3}をお{願い|ねがい}できますか。
phrases.en: Could I have a receipt, please?
phrases.note: {領収書|りょうしゅうしょ} is the formal receipt; レシート is the shop slip.

phrases.jp: {雪道|ゆきみち|snowy road|3}は、{僕|ぼく}にとってまだ{怖い|こわい}です。
phrases.en: Snowy roads are still scary for me.
phrases.note: Person + にとって = from that person's point of view.

dialogue_setting: アルちゃん tells the story of his Monday in {長野市|ながのし}; the taxi driver's words are quoted.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {月曜日|げつようび}、スキーの{手袋|てぶくろ}とゴーグルを{買いに|かいに}、{電車|でんしゃ}で{長野市|ながのし}へ{行った|いった}。
dialogue.en: On Monday I took the train to {長野市|ながのし} to buy ski gloves and goggles.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {駅前|えきまえ}でタクシーに{乗って|のって}、スマホの{地図|ちず}を{見せた|みせた}。「この{住所|じゅうしょ|address|3}までお{願い|ねがい}します」
dialogue.en: In front of the station I got in a taxi and showed my phone map. 'To this address, please.'

dialogue.speaker: 運転手さん
dialogue.jp: 「お{客|きゃく}さん、ここから{歩いて|あるいて}5{分|ふん}ですよ」
dialogue.en: 'Sir, it's a five-minute walk from here,' the driver laughed.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: でも{雪道|ゆきみち|snowy road|3}は、スペインから{来た|きた}{僕|ぼく}にとってまだ{怖い|こわい}。{運転手|うんてんしゅ|(taxi) driver|4}さんにとっては{普通|ふつう}らしいけど。
dialogue.en: But for me, from Spain, snowy roads are still scary. For the driver it's normal, apparently.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: だから{乗せて|のせて|to give (someone) a ride|3}もらった。{最後|さいご}に「{次|つぎ}の{信号|しんごう|traffic light|4}で{止めて|とめて|to stop (something)|4}もらえますか」と{頼んだ|たのんだ}。
dialogue.en: So he gave me a ride. At the end I asked, 'Could you stop at the next light?'

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {帰り|かえり|the way back|4}の{電車|でんしゃ}で、レンさんのことを{考えた|かんがえた}。{同じ|おなじ}{町|まち}にいたのに、{連絡|れんらく}する{勇気|ゆうき|courage|3}がなかった。
dialogue.en: On the train back, I thought about レン. We were in the same city, but I didn't have the courage to message him.

listening.intro: The driver's last words as you get out. Type what he says.

lines.jp: {着きました|つきました}よ。{足元|あしもと|one's step, footing|3}に{気をつけて|きをつけて}ください。
lines.en: Here we are. Watch your step.

grammar.meaning: for (someone), from their point of view
grammar.form: noun + にとって ({僕|ぼく}にとって, {子|こ}どもにとって) · contrast: noun + にとっては ({運転手|うんてんしゅ}さんにとっては) · before a noun: noun + にとっての + noun ({私|わたし}にとっての{家族|かぞく})
grammar.explanation: How something is from someone's point of view, with words like {大切|たいせつ}, {難|むずか}しい, {怖|こわ}い. It's not for doing something for someone (that's のために), and not に{対|たい}して, which marks a target.
mark: 運転手さんにとっては

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}は、{私|わたし}にとって{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.en: My family is the most important thing to me.

examples.jp: この{本|ほん}は、{子|こ}どもにとって{少し|すこし}{難しい|むずかしい}。
examples.en: This book is a bit difficult for children.

quiz.question: {田中|たなか}さん＿＿、りんごの{木|き}は{子|こ}どものようなものだ。
quiz.en: For {田中|たなか}さん, the apple trees are like his children.
quiz.explain: From his point of view → にとって. について would mean 'about {田中|たなか}さん'.

quiz_more.question: {健康|けんこう|health|3}＿＿、{毎日|まいにち}{歩いて|あるいて}います。
quiz_more.en: I walk every day for my health.
quiz_more.explain: A goal you act for → のために. にとって is a point of view, not a purpose.

quiz_more.question: {日本人|にほんじん}＿＿{普通|ふつう}のことでも、{外国人|がいこくじん}には{不思議|ふしぎ|strange, mysterious|3}なことがある。
quiz_more.en: Some things are normal for Japanese people but strange to foreigners.
quiz_more.explain: Normal from Japanese people's point of view → にとって.

kanji.where: The red sign lit up behind the windscreen of the taxis waiting at {長野駅|ながのえき}.
kanji.breakdown: {空車|くうしゃ}: 空 empty + 車 car → 'empty car': this taxi is free.
kanji.related: {賃走|ちんそう} = occupied, meter running; {迎車|げいしゃ} = on its way to pick someone up.

tip.title: Hands off the taxi door
tip.body: Japanese taxi doors open and close by themselves: the driver works them, so don't touch. In small towns there are few taxis, so call one (タクシーを{呼|よ}ぶ) or wait at the station. No tipping.

challenge.prompt: {健太|けんた} on LINE: 「{長野|ながの}どうやった？」 You want to say it was fun, but snowy roads are still scary for you. One part is wrong.

parts.jp: {楽しかった|たのしかった}けど、

parts.why: について means 'about me'. From your point of view → にとって.

challenge.model_answer: {楽しかった|たのしかった}けど、{雪道|ゆきみち|snowy road|3}は{僕|ぼく}にとってまだ{怖い|こわい}な。
challenge.explanation: {僕|ぼく}にとって frames {怖|こわ}い from your point of view: scary for you, not for everyone. けど turns from the fun part to the scary part. Plain form + な fits a chat with {健太|けんた}.
challenge.hint: noun + にとって = from someone's point of view

vocab.note: {住|じゅう} live + {所|しょ} place. Forms ask for {住所|じゅうしょ} and {氏名|しめい} (full name).
Say {運転手|うんてんしゅ}さん to the driver. {手|しゅ} = person doing it.

vocab.en: to give a ride; to put on
vocab.note: {乗|の}る = you get on; {乗|の}せる = someone takes you. {乗|の}せてもらう = get a lift.
A green light is {青|あお} in Japanese: {信号|しんごう}が{青|あお}になった.
{止|と}まる = it stops; {止|と}める = you stop it. Also: park a car.
{帰|かえ}りの{電車|でんしゃ} = the train home. {行|い}き = the way there.
{勇気|ゆうき}がない = can't bring yourself to. {勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}す = pluck up courage.
For work expenses. Often with a name on it: お{名前|なまえ}は？

kanji_study.parts: 亠 a lid or roof + 巾 cloth → cloth stalls under a roof: a market, and the town that grew round it: city.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 布 (cloth): 布 has ナ on top, 市 has 亠.

kanji_study.parts: 口 mouth + a bent line under it → a voice shouting out a call: a signal, and the numbers that are called out.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 写 (copy): 号 has 口 on top, 写 has 冖.

extras.title: Taking a taxi
extras.title_jp: タクシーの{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: What you'll hear and say in a Japanese taxi.

items.note: To get out a little early.

items.jp: {急いで|いそいで}もらえますか。
items.note: Polite request with 〜てもらえますか.

items.jp: タクシー{乗り場|のりば|taxi rank|3}
items.note: {乗|の}り{場|ば} = boarding place. Also バス{乗|の}り{場|ば}.

extras.title: Three kinds of 'for'
extras.intro: English 'for' has three different Japanese forms.

items.jp: {僕|ぼく}にとって{大切|たいせつ}
items.note: Point of view → にとって.

items.jp: {僕|ぼく}のために{作った|つくった}
items.note: Benefit or purpose → のために.

items.jp: {僕|ぼく}に{対して|たいして}{優しい|やさしい}
items.note: Target of an attitude → に{対|たい}して.
